name: confounded_late_drift
description: A second confounded world, deliberately unlike the first. Scenario G confounds an edge-uniformity fault that a metrology channel reads directly; this confounds a *parametric drift*, whose evidence is a slow move in the process summaries, and it does so late in the horizon with a dedication window that starts before the fault and outlasts it. One product is preferentially routed to the drifting chamber's tool from day 40 to day 75 at a share of 0.8, while the fault itself begins at day 45 and ramps over a fortnight. Because the window opens first, an engine that reads the routing shift as the change point will find a product and a tool that both moved and a chamber that moved later — the ordering is the evidence, and getting it wrong is the mistake this scenario is built to catch. The routing shift is honest observable data in `runs`, as ADR-015 requires; the drift is not.
